questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply **BODMAS** rule: Solve **Bracket** first, then **Multiplication**.

62 + 83 − 38 + (50) × 2 − 89

62 + 83 − 38 + 100 − 89

145 + 100 − 38 − 89 = 245 − 127 = 118

**∴ The correct answer is 118.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 62 + 83 − 38 + (36 + 14) × 2 − 89

**Formula:** Follow the **BODMAS** hierarchy (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

⇒ 62 + 83 − 38 + (50) × 2 − 89

⇒ 62 + 83 − 38 + 100 − 89

⇒ (62 + 83 + 100) − (38 + 89)

⇒ 245 − 127

⇒ 118

**∴ The correct answer is 118.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

VBODMAS Rule

This rule specifies the order: **Vinculum** (bar), **Bracket**, **Of**, **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

Types of Brackets

Always solve in the order: **Parentheses** ( ), **Braces** { }, and then **Square Brackets** [ ].

Addition and Subtraction

For addition and subtraction, grouping **positive** and **negative** terms separately before the final calculation minimizes errors.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve using the **VBODMAS** rule: handle **Brackets** and **Division** first.

45 + 31 − 16 + 54 + 38 − 21

Group **positive** and **negative** terms: (45 + 31 + 54 + 38) − (16 + 21)

168 − 37 = 131

**∴ The correct answer is 131.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 45 + 62 ÷ 2 − 16 + (27 × 2) + 38 − 21

**Rule Used:** **BODMAS** (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 45 + 62 ÷ 2 − 16 + 54 + 38 − 21 (Solving **Bracket**: 27 × 2)

⇒ 45 + 31 − 16 + 54 + 38 − 21 (Solving **Division**: 62 ÷ 2)

⇒ 76 − 16 + 54 + 38 − 21

⇒ 168 − 16 − 21 (Performing **Addition**)

⇒ 168 − 37 (Performing **Subtraction**)

⇒ 131

**∴ The correct answer is 131.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

VBODMAS Rule

It stands for **Vinculum**, **Bracket**, **Of**, **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**, defining the correct sequence for mathematical operations.

Grouping Positives and Negatives

To minimize errors during **Addition** and **Subtraction**, sum all positive numbers together and all negative numbers together before finding the final difference.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve each term by observing decimal places: ³√0.027 = 0.3

Square root term: √0.49 = 0.7

Next cube root terms: ³√0.064 = 0.4 and ³√0.216 = 0.6

Combine results: 0.3 + 0.7 + 0.4 − 0.6 = 0.8

**∴ The correct answer is 0.8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** ³√0.027 + √0.49 + ³√0.064 − ³√0.216

**Method:** Convert **decimals to fractions** for easier root extraction.

⇒ ³√(27/1000) + √(49/100) + ³√(64/1000) − ³√(216/1000)

⇒ (3/10) + (7/10) + (4/10) − (6/10)

⇒ 0.3 + 0.7 + 0.4 − 0.6

⇒ 1.0 + 0.4 − 0.6

⇒ 1.4 − 0.6

⇒ 0.8

**∴ The correct answer is 0.8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cube Root of Decimals

For a cube root, if the original number has 3n decimal places, the result will have n decimal places. Example: ³√0.001 = 0.1.

Square Root of Decimals

For a square root, if the original number has 2n decimal places, the result will have n decimal places. Example: √0.01 = 0.1.

Common Cubes to Remember

Quick recall of 3³ = 27, 4³ = 64, and 6³ = 216 is essential for competitive **Simplification** questions.

questions.question: If √306.25 = 17.5, then what is the value of √0.00000030625?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given that √306.25 = 17.5, the **significant digits** of the square root of 30625 are **175**.

In **square roots**, the number of **decimal places** in the result is exactly **half** of those in the original number.

The given value 0.000000030625 (assuming the standard 12-place structure for the provided answer) has **12 decimal places**.

Therefore, the square root must have 12 ÷ 2 = **6 decimal places**.

Applying this to 175: we get **0.000175**.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.000175.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** √306.25 = 17.5

**Formula Used:** √(a × 10−²ⁿ) = √a × 10−ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/019dc9b6aa513f4963b01a29015bfe07e2843b7938fce506e58e6b7213e1d9f3.png] 

⇒ √306.25 = 17.5

⇒ √(30625 ÷ 100) = 175 ÷ 10

⇒ √30625 = 175

⇒ √0.000000030625 = √(30625 × 10−¹²)

⇒ √30625 × √10−¹²

⇒ 175 × 10−⁶

⇒ 175 × 0.000001 = 0.000175

**∴ The correct answer is 0.000175.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root of Decimals

The number of digits after the decimal point in the square root of a perfect square decimal is exactly **half** the number of digits after the decimal point in the original number.

Power of 10 Rule

When calculating √10−ⁿ, if n is an even integer, the result is 10−ⁿ/². This is why the number of zeros effectively doubles when squaring and halves when taking a root.

Perfect Squares ending in 25

To find √30625, split it as 306|25. The 25 gives 5. For 306, find two consecutive integers whose product is 306 (17 × 18 = 306). The smaller number is 17. Thus, the root is 175.

questions.question: sqrt{(0.16)/(0.0004)} times sqrt{(0.25)/(0.49)} = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

First, simplify the **decimals**: 0.16/0.0004 is equivalent to 1600/4 = 400.

The **Square root** of 400 is 20.

Next, simplify √(0.25/0.49) as √(25/49), which equals 5/7.

Multiply the results: 20 × 5/7 = 100/7.

**∴ The correct answer is 100/7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Equation:** √(0.16/0.0004) × √(0.25/0.49)

**Formula Used:** √(a/b) = √a / √b

⇒ √((16/100) ÷ (4/10000)) × √((25/100) ÷ (49/100))

⇒ √((16/100) × (10000/4)) × √(25/49)

⇒ √(4 × 100) × (5/7)

⇒ √400 × (5/7)

⇒ 20 × (5/7)

⇒ 100/7

**∴ The correct answer is 100/7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root Properties

For any positive numbers a and b, √(a × b) = √a × √b and √(a/b) = √a / √b.

Decimal Manipulation

To simplify **decimal fractions**, multiply the numerator and denominator by 10ⁿ to shift the decimal point until whole numbers are obtained.

Perfect Squares

Recognizing **perfect squares** like 16, 25, 49, and 400 helps in fast calculation of square roots during competitive exams.

questions.question: The side of a square is 15 cm. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the square?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Perimeter** of a **square** is calculated as 4 × side.

Given side = 15 cm.

Perimeter = 4 × 15 = 60 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the **square** (a) = 15 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Perimeter** of square = 4 × a

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4ccf4a8b0b610e8bcf05140681dbdb432b9abb9e7e9628c47655f2282af6e5c7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Perimeter** = 4 × 15

⇒ **Perimeter** = 60 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 60 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Square

The total space enclosed by a square is called its area. Area = side² = a².

Diagonal of a Square

The length of the diagonal connecting opposite vertices. Diagonal = side × √2 = a√2.

Properties of a Square

All four sides are equal, all internal angles are 90°, and diagonals bisect each other at right angles.

questions.question: The length and breadth of a rectangle is 9 cm and 4 cm respectively. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Perimeter** of a **Rectangle** is twice the sum of its **Length** and **Breadth**.

Sum of sides = 9 + 4 = 13 cm.

Perimeter = 2 × 13 = 26 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 26 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Length** of the **Rectangle** (L) = 9 cm

**Breadth** of the **Rectangle** (B) = 4 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Perimeter** (P) = 2 × (L + B)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c17208277cdc209f96691669cecdcdb294c9880bedec6eb798ebf3d2c47a802f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ P = 2 × (9 + 4)

⇒ P = 2 × 13

⇒ P = 26 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 26 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rectangle

The total space occupied by the rectangle is given by **Area** = Length × Breadth (L × B).

Diagonal of Rectangle

The distance between opposite corners is found using the **Pythagoras theorem**: Diagonal = √(L² + B²).

Perimeter of Square

A **Square** is a special rectangle where all sides are equal. Its **Perimeter** = 4 × Side.

questions.question: Which of the following number is neither divisible by 4 nor by 9?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the number where the **last two digits** are not divisible by **4** AND the **sum of digits** is not divisible by **9**.

For **10263**: Last two digits are **63** (not divisible by 4).

Sum of digits = 1 + 0 + 2 + 6 + 3 = **12** (not divisible by 9).

**∴ The correct answer is 10263.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers 10263, 10260, 10116, 10296.

**Method:** Apply **divisibility rules** for 4 and 9.

⇒ **Divisibility rule of 4:** Last two digits must be divisible by 4.

⇒ **Divisibility rule of 9:** Sum of all digits must be divisible by 9.

⇒ **10263:** Last two digits 63 (63 ÷ 4 → Remainder 3). Sum = 1 + 0 + 2 + 6 + 3 = 12 (12 ÷ 9 → Remainder 3). Neither divisible by 4 nor 9.

⇒ **10260:** Last two digits 60 (60 ÷ 4 = 15). Sum = 1 + 0 + 2 + 6 + 0 = 9 (9 ÷ 9 = 1). Divisible by both 4 and 9.

⇒ **10116:** Last two digits 16 (16 ÷ 4 = 4). Sum = 1 + 0 + 1 + 1 + 6 = 9 (9 ÷ 9 = 1). Divisible by both 4 and 9.

⇒ **10296:** Last two digits 96 (96 ÷ 4 = 24). Sum = 1 + 0 + 2 + 9 + 6 = 18 (18 ÷ 9 = 2). Divisible by both 4 and 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 10263.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 3.

Divisibility by 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the **last three digits** of the number are divisible by 8.

Divisibility by 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the **sum of digits at odd positions** and the **sum of digits at even positions** is 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.question: 2[(412)² + (188)²] - (412 - 188)² = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Recognize the **Algebraic Identity**: 2(a² + b²) − (a − b)² = (a + b)².

Here, let **a = 412** and **b = 188**.

The expression simplifies to (412 + 188)² = 600².

600 × 600 = 360000.

**∴ The correct answer is 360000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png]

questions.question: Average of 14 numbers is 45. Average of 5 numbers among them is 'x'. Average of the remaining numbers is 35. What is the value of 'x'?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total deviation must be **zero** from the **mean (45)**.

Deviation of 9 remaining numbers = (35 − 45) × 9 = −90.

To balance this, the 5 numbers must have a total deviation of +90.

Average deviation for 5 numbers = 90 ÷ 5 = +18.

Value of **x** = 45 + 18 = 63.

**∴ The correct answer is 63.**

questions.question: A is smallest 3 digit number divisible by both 12 and 15. B is the largest 3 digit number divisible by 12 and 15. What is the value of B - A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**LCM** of 12 and 15 = **60**.

Smallest 3-digit multiple of 60 is **A = 120** (60 × 2).

Largest 3-digit multiple of 60 is **B = 960** (60 × 16).

Required value **B − A = 960 − 120 = 840**.

**∴ The correct answer is 840.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = 12 and 15

**Formula used:**

Any number divisible by both 12 and 15 must be a multiple of their **Least Common Multiple (LCM)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/88e191ae2cad3ffb5ba62a738430f90f180ed6382362894898382b023d9b7aac.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factors of 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ Prime factors of 15 = 3 × 5

⇒ **LCM(12, 15)** = 2² × 3 × 5 = **60**

⇒ Smallest 3-digit number (starting from 100) divisible by 60:

⇒ 100 ÷ 60 ≈ 1.66 → next multiple is 60 × 2 = **120 (A)**

⇒ Largest 3-digit number (ending at 999) divisible by 60:

⇒ 999 ÷ 60 ≈ 16.65 → largest multiple is 60 × 16 = **960 (B)**

⇒ Required value = B − A = 960 − 120 = **840**

**∴ The correct answer is 840.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and Multiples

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of two or more numbers is the smallest non-zero common multiple of those numbers. Any common multiple of a and b is always a multiple of LCM(a, b).

Divisibility by 60

A number is divisible by **60** if it is simultaneously divisible by 3, 4, and 5. This property is useful for checking calculations involving minutes and seconds.

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers x and y: **x × y = HCF(x, y) × LCM(x, y)**. Here, HCF(12, 15) = 3 and LCM(12, 15) = 60, so 12 × 15 = 3 × 60 = 180.

questions.question: There are 3 classes A, B and C. There are 36, 60 and 72 students in these classes respectively. Each class is to be divided into groups. Each group has same number of students. Each group should have students from only one class. Every student is a part of 1 group. What is the maximum number of students in each group?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ To find the **maximum number of students** in each group, find the **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** of the students in each class. Step 1: Find the **differences** between the numbers: (60 − 36) = 24 and (72 − 60) = 12. Step 2: The **HCF** is either the smallest difference or its factor. Step 3: Check if 12 divides all: 36 ÷ 12 = 3, 60 ÷ 12 = 5, 72 ÷ 12 = 6. All are divisible, so the **HCF is 12**. **∴ The correct answer is 12 students.**

questions.question: A person paid Rs. 36 as tax on an article worth Rs. 900. What is the rate of tax?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Compare the **Tax Amount** with the **Article Worth** using the unitary method.

100% of the value = ₹900

1% of the value = 900 ÷ 100 = ₹9

Since ₹9 is 1%, then ₹36 is (36 ÷ 9) × 1% = 4%.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The **Article Worth** = ₹900

The **Tax Paid** = ₹36

**Formula Used:**

Rate of Tax = (Tax Amount ÷ Article Worth) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4a5905e631d0457da1fd81ad988dfd12766ab4586ec0d41b9932eeebe13a4d5b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Tax Rate = (36 ÷ 900) × 100

⇒ Tax Rate = (36 ÷ 9)

⇒ Tax Rate = 4%

**∴ The correct answer is 4 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sales Tax and VAT

Tax is an additional amount calculated on the **Selling Price** of an item. Formula: Tax = (Tax Rate ÷ 100) × Selling Price.

Effective Price Calculation

The total amount paid by the customer is the **Net Price**. Net Price = Original Price + Tax Amount.

Percentage Rule

To find what percentage one number is of another, use the ratio: (Part ÷ Total) × 100.

questions.question: An article is sold for a profit of Rs. 120. Profit percentage is 30 percent. What is the selling price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given that 30% of **Profit** corresponds to ₹120.

1% of **Cost Price** = 120 ÷ 30 = ₹4

**Selling Price** (SP) = **Cost Price** (100%) + **Profit** (30%) = 130%

130% of **Cost Price** = 130 × 4 = ₹520

**∴ The correct answer is ₹520.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Profit** = ₹120

**Profit percentage** = 30%

**Formula Used:**

**Profit** = **Selling Price** − **Cost Price**

**Profit %** = (**Profit** ÷ **Cost Price**) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/19f01b992517fe9414c66de77ee5ce726f5dcb7ba8e7ded124785a10e01abe2e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 30% of **Cost Price** = 120

⇒ **Cost Price** = (120 × 100) ÷ 30

⇒ **Cost Price** = 4 × 100 = ₹400

⇒ **Selling Price** = **Cost Price** + **Profit**

⇒ **Selling Price** = 400 + 120 = ₹520

**∴ The correct answer is ₹520.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP)

The price at which an article is purchased. It is always considered as the base (100%) for calculating profit or loss percentage.

Loss Percentage

When SP < CP, **Loss %** = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100. It indicates the percentage reduction from the original cost.

Marked Price (MP) and Discount

MP is the price printed on the label. **Discount** = MP − SP. **Discount %** is always calculated on the **Marked Price**.

questions.question: A person earns 25 percent profit on selling price. What is the ratio of the value of the profit to the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit = 25% of **Selling Price (SP)** = 1/4 of SP.

If SP = 4 units, then Profit = 1 unit.

**Cost Price (CP)** = SP − Profit = 4 − 1 = 3 units.

Ratio of **Profit : Cost Price** = 1 : 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Profit percentage on **Selling Price** = 25%

**Formula Used:** Cost Price = Selling Price − Profit | Ratio = Profit / Cost Price

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/35493509d1aa04e893c14ff060de973a638b36e7cca72ae4fd522b3c5b1d896e.png] 

⇒ Let the **Selling Price (SP)** = 100

⇒ **Profit** = 25% of SP = 25

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = SP − Profit = 100 − 25 = 75

⇒ Required Ratio = Profit : CP

⇒ Required Ratio = 25 : 75

⇒ Required Ratio = 1 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage on CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100. This is the standard way to calculate profit unless specified otherwise.

Relationship between SP and CP

If Profit is x/y of SP, then Profit is x/(y−x) of CP. Here, 1/4 of SP = 1/(4−1) = 1/3 of CP.

Marked Price (MP) and Discount

Selling Price = Marked Price − Discount. Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price**.

questions.question: A person spends 40 percent of his income. His income increases by 50 percent and expenditure increases by 40 percent. The increased saving is Rs. 4700. What is his initial income?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **initial income** = 100 units. Then **expenditure** = 40 units and **savings** = 60 units.

**New income** = 150 units (50% increase).

**New expenditure** = 40 × 1.4 = 56 units (40% increase).

**New savings** = 150 − 56 = 94 units.

According to the question, 94 units = ₹4700 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹50.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **expenditure** = 40% of **income**.

Increase in **income** = 50%.

Increase in **expenditure** = 40%.

Increased **saving** = ₹4700.

**Formula used:**

**Income** = **Expenditure** + **Saving**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cc91ecd01274744f16d2dc734c83c93f84202faf41d8cf0fd5d73bd0d51ad13a.png] 

Let the **initial income** be 100x.

⇒ Initial **expenditure** = 40x

⇒ Initial **savings** = 100x − 40x = 60x

⇒ **New income** = 100x + 50% of 100x = 150x

⇒ **New expenditure** = 40x + 40% of 40x

⇒ **New expenditure** = 40x + 16x = 56x

⇒ **New savings** = 150x − 56x = 94x

⇒ Given: 94x = 4700

⇒ x = 4700 ÷ 94

⇒ x = 50

⇒ **Initial income** = 100 × 50 = ₹5000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure, and Saving Relationship

The fundamental equation for income-based problems is: **Income = Expenditure + Savings**. Any percentage change in one component affects the others based on this balance.

Percentage Increase Shortcut

To increase a value by a%, multiply the original value by (100 + a)/100. For example, a 40% increase means multiplying by 1.40.

Net Effect on Savings

If income increases by x% and expenditure increases by y%, the percentage change in savings depends on the initial ratio of expenditure to savings. Weighted averages can also be used here.

questions.question: A is 2 times as good a workman as B. A and B together can finish a work in 24 days. In how many days will B alone complete the same work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Efficiency ratio** of A : B = 2 : 1

Total efficiency of **(A + B)** = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day

**Total Work** = Combined Efficiency × Time = 3 × 24 = 72 units

Time taken by **B alone** = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B = 72 ÷ 1 = 72 days

**∴ The correct answer is 72 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Efficiency of **A** is 2 times that of **B**.

Time taken by **A** and **B** together = 24 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time taken

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of **B** be 1 unit/day.

⇒ Efficiency of **A** = 2 × 1 = 2 units/day.

⇒ Combined efficiency of **A** and **B** = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day.

⇒ **Total Work** = Combined Efficiency × Time = 3 × 24 = 72 units.

⇒ Days taken by **B** alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Days taken by **B** = 72 ÷ 1 = 72 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 72 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete a work. If the ratio of efficiency is x : y, the ratio of time taken will be y : x.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the **ratio of work done** or the **ratio of efficiencies** if the time period of work is the same for all workers.

Pipes and Cisterns

The same logic applies where **filling rate** is considered positive efficiency and **emptying rate** (leakage) is considered negative efficiency.

questions.question: R, M and T work for 6 days, 8 days and 10 days respectively. They get a total amount of Rs. 760 for their work. Ratio of one day work of R, M and T is 2 : 3 : 4 respectively. How much money (in Rs.) does M get?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Total Work Done** = (Days × One day work efficiency)

R : M : T = (6 × 2) : (8 × 3) : (10 × 4) = 12 : 24 : 40

Simplified **Work Ratio** = 3 : 6 : 10 (Dividing by 4)

Total units = 3 + 6 + 10 = 19 units → ₹760

M's Share = (6 ÷ 19) × 760 = 6 × 40 = ₹240

**∴ The correct answer is ₹240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Working days of **R, M, and T** = 6, 8, and 10 days respectively.

Ratio of **Efficiency** (One day work) = 2 : 3 : 4

Total **Wages** received = ₹760

**Formula Used:**

Total Share of Money ∝ Total Work Done (Days × Efficiency)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab4dde7319a0fe3ae8a74fbf82ea245ebb1133a9851b3c179127d55d10d50a41.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Share of R = 6 × 2 = 12 units

⇒ Share of M = 8 × 3 = 24 units

⇒ Share of T = 10 × 4 = 40 units

⇒ Ratio of shares = 12 : 24 : 40

⇒ Ratio of shares = 3 : 6 : 10

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 3 + 6 + 10 = 19 units

⇒ 19 units = ₹760

⇒ 1 unit = 760 ÷ 19 = ₹40

⇒ M's total money = 6 × 40 = ₹240

**∴ The correct answer is ₹240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Wages and Work Done

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the **total work done** by each individual, which is the product of their **efficiency** and the **time** they worked.

Efficiency Formula

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Total Time. If the work is constant, efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken.

Work and Wages Variation

If multiple people work for the same duration, their wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their **one-day efficiency**.

questions.question: B covers a distance of 42 km in 7 hours. C covers the distance of 108 km in 9 hours. What is the ratio of speed of B to the speed of C?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed of **B** = 42 ÷ 7 = 6 kmph

Speed of **C** = 108 ÷ 9 = 12 kmph

Required Ratio = 6 : 12 = 1 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance covered by **B** = 42 km

Time taken by **B** = 7 hr

Distance covered by **C** = 108 km

Time taken by **C** = 9 hr

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67d7de4ae9e9282b24f7cfb75c4fd77eb3a8cc3a2aa92f20bb7702fb98ffe4ad.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of **B** (SB) = 42 ÷ 7

⇒ SB = 6 kmph

⇒ Speed of **C** (SC) = 108 ÷ 9

⇒ SC = 12 kmph

⇒ Ratio = SB : SC

⇒ Ratio = 6 : 12

⇒ Ratio = 1 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert kmph to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to kmph, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If distances are equal, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x+y), where x and y are individual speeds.

Relative Speed

When moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

questions.question: S travels with 90 percent of his usual speed and reaches his home 10 minutes late. What is the usual time (in minutes) taken by him to reach home?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ **Speed ratio** (Usual : New) = 100 : 90 = 10 : 9 Since **Distance** is constant, **Time ratio** is inverse of Speed ratio = 9 : 10 Difference in time ratio parts = 10 − 9 = 1 unit Given, 1 unit = 10 min **Usual time** = 9 units = 9 × 10 = 90 min **∴ The correct answer is 90 min.**
